claims.text: High-entropy alloys exhibit high solid-solution strengthening.
Solid-solution strengthening improves HEA tribological properties through increased strength and corrosion resistance.
Increased strength and corrosion resistance reduce microstructural changes under tribological loading.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a single-phase microstructure.
CoCrFeMnNi is subjected to dry, reciprocating tribological loading under a mild normal load.
Testing is conducted at room temperature, 50% relative humidity, and a sliding speed of 0.5 mm s−1.
Tribological loading produces a subsurface deformation microstructure containing nanocrystalline grains, twins, and bands of localized dislocation motion.
Localized dislocation activity associated with planar slip causes grain rotation.
Twin fragmentation and dislocation rearrangement produce a nanocrystalline layer beneath the worn surface.
Lattice distortion and stacking-fault energy influence deformation and dislocation-mediated behavior in CoCrFeMnNi.
Solid-solution strengthening is the governing cause of reduced subsurface microstructural change in CoCrFeMnNi.
CoCrFeMnNi will have a lower wear rate than the conventional-alloy baseline.
CoCrFeMnNi will have a lower corrosion rate than the conventional-alloy baseline under the stated loading conditions.
Conventional steel provides a lower-entropy baseline with a simpler microstructure.
The response may vary with HEA composition, microstructure, and tribological conditions.
Precipitation strengthening or grain-boundary sliding may also influence tribological behavior.
CoCrFeMnNi and steel will be compared under identical test conditions while measuring wear rate, corrosion rate, and microstructural changes.
Failure of CoCrFeMnNi to show significantly improved tribological properties relative to steel would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The experiment specifies dry sliding but predicts and proposes measuring a corrosion-rate component. Without an electrolyte or another defined corrosive environment, the design does not implement tribo-corrosion or permit separation of coupled wear and corrosion contributions.
